name: web/scene-3d
title: 3D scene
summary: One HTML file with a three.js 3D scene made from plain lines: things (kiwi, tree, house, car and about 60 more) and what they do (walks to, runs to, flies to, drives to, follows, orbits).
when: Use when the user wants something in 3D, a three.js or WebGL page, a 3D simulation, or an animated scene of things that walk, drive or fly.

title.about: A short name for the scene, shown in the browser tab and on the page.

scene.about:
What the user asked for, as plain lines separated by 
: one thing or one action per line, no code. A thing: "house at 5 -1". An action: "dog walks to house" (also runs to, flies to, drives to, follows, orbits). For "a dog comes home" the value is "house at 5 -1
dog at -7 2
dog walks to house".
scene.default:
house at 5 -1
tree at -2 -4
dog at -7 2
dog walks to house

sky.about: The sky: day, dawn, sunset or night.

ground.about: The ground: grass, sand, snow, water, stone, dirt or moon.

next: The page is finished and shows itself in the chat; it needs no build, no npm and no server. To change the scene, edit only the plain lines inside <script id="scene"> in index.html with replace_in_file, for example the line "sky day" (the comment above them lists every thing and action). Do not rewrite the file.
